The mapped_rxn string: '[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

So product SMILES is after >>: '[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

So it's a cyclohexene? Let's approximate product SMILES: "COC(=O)C1(/C=C/c2ccccc2)C= C1[Si](C)(C)C". Need correct. The ring: C5 is carbonyl carbon? Wait C5 is carbon attached to carbonyl carbon? The carbonyl carbon is C3? Actually [CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4]) is methyl ester carbonyl carbon (C3). Then [C:5]1(... ) is attached to carbonyl carbon? So product is methyl 5-(trimethylsilyl)cyclohex-2-ene-1-carboxylate? plus phenyl? The aromatic part is c:8 attached to ring via /[CH]=[CH]/[c]2... So it's a phenyl substituent.

Thus product SMILES maybe: "COC(=O)C1(/C=C/c2ccccc2)C= C1[Si](C)(C)C". Let's generate: "COC(=O)C1(/C=C/c2ccccc2)C= C1[Si](C)(C)C". Need proper SMILES: "COC(=O)C1(/C=C/c2ccccc2)C= C1[Si](C)(C)C". Remove spaces: "COC(=O)C1(/C=C/c2ccccc2)C=C1[Si](C)(C)C". That seems plausible.
